newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Bonte seen between 8.75 pct and 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Bonte seen between 8.75 pct and 9.0 pct.

text.p: Argentina's issue of $750 million in five year Bonte Treasury bonds is expected to be placed at a cut-off yield of between 8.75 percent and 9.0 percent, market players said Monday.

Half of the six traders called by Reuters saw a rate of 8.75 percent and the other half forecast 9.0 percent at Tuesday's auction. A yield around those levels would be below Argentina's FRB Brady bond maturing in 2005, which currently has a yield to maturity of around 9.51 percent. It would also be below the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002, which has a yield to maturity of about 9.14 percent. Argentina's Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 yields 8.33 percent.
The head trader at an Argentine bank said the Bonte auction would be successful judging by the fact the Economy Ministry decided to issue $750 million rather than the widely expected $500 million.
Tuesday's auction is the first tranche of the bond that matures on May 9, 2002. It will be raised to a total $2.0 billion in later tranches to make the instrument more liquid.

This is the longest maturity Bonte to be issued in the local market through the market-maker system set up last April. The longest maturity Bonte now in circulation is two years. It yields 7.86 percent.
